entries.title: How living things change over generations
entries.answer: Living things often have small differences from others of the same kind. Suppose some beetles have a color that makes it harder for birds to spot them. If young beetles can inherit that color and beetles with it tend to have more young, the helpful color may become more common in later generations. That is one way evolution can happen. Evolution is change in a group over generations. It does not mean one beetle changes its kind while it grows up. Changes can build up in a group over a long time.

sections.heading: What is an adaptation?
sections.text: An adaptation is a feature that helps living things survive or have young in the place where they live. A feature that helps in one place might make less difference somewhere else.

facts: Natural selection is one way evolution can happen.
Fossils are some of the evidence scientists use to study evolution.

entries.title: Tyrannosaurus rex
entries.answer: Tyrannosaurus rex was a large dinosaur that walked on two back legs. Some adults reached about 40 feet long. A long tail helped balance the weight of the big head and body. Its thick teeth and strong jaws could crush bone, which helps scientists work out what it could eat. The two short arms each ended in two clawed fingers. Its fossils come from western North America. T. rex lived near the end of the time when large dinosaurs walked the land.
facts: Tyrannosaurus rex lived toward the end of the Cretaceous Period.

entries.title: What fossils tell us
entries.answer: A fossil is something from long-ago life that lasts into the present. It might be part of a shell or a tooth, or a mark left by a leaf or a walking animal. Fossils can form when sand or mud quickly covers a body or a mark and protects it. Over time, the layers may harden into rock. A footprint can show how an animal walked, even if no bones of that animal were found nearby. Scientists look at fossils and the rocks around them to learn about life long before people kept records.
facts: Bones and shells are often better preserved than soft body parts.
A dinosaur track can be a fossil even though it is not a piece of the dinosaur.

entries.title: What happened to most dinosaurs
entries.answer: About 66 million years ago, most kinds of dinosaurs disappeared. Scientists have strong evidence that a huge asteroid hit Earth at about that time. The impact left a wide crater near what is now the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico. Dust and other material from the crash spread through the air and reduced the sunlight that reached the ground. That made it harder for plants to grow and broke up the food supply of many animals. Some living things survived, including ancestors of the birds we see today.
facts: A thin layer of rock in many places contains signs of the impact.
All dinosaurs outside the bird branch died out.

entries.title: Why birds are living dinosaurs
entries.answer: Birds belong to one branch of the dinosaur family. Their early relatives were small, two-legged dinosaurs that lived long before people. Scientists see clues to that family link in fossils. Some dinosaurs that were not birds had feathers. Some also had bones or feet that share details with those of early birds. This does not mean a chicken came directly from Tyrannosaurus rex. Birds and T. rex are more like distant cousins, and their family branches go back to an older group of meat-eating dinosaurs.
facts: Some dinosaur feathers existed before birds could fly.
The bird branch survived after the other dinosaur branches died out.
